in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my child Alex, who is 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 19 years old, eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether they are in approved education or training. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training.

Could you please tell me if Alex is currently in approved education or training (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or similar full-time non-advanced education)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. A-levels count as approved education, so that's positive for eligibility.

I have a couple more questions:

Does Alex work at all? Specifically, does Alex work 24 hours or more per week in paid employment?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he does work. He has a part-time job at the supermarket - it's actually full-time hours, so yes, more than 24 hours a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is important information.

Unfortunately, working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment affects eligibility for Child Benefit, even if the child is still in approved education or training. 

Just to confirm one more thing: Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

I also need to ask a few questions about your own circumstances:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful.

Just one more question to complete the assessment: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, yes actually - his mum already claims it and he lives with her too.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail.

So just to make sure I understand correctly: Alex lives with both you and his mum (perhaps in a shared arrangement), and his mum is already receiving Child Benefit for him?

Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at any one time. If Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to also receive it unless she stopped her claim.

However, there's also another issue: since Alex works 24 hours or more per week in paid employment, this would stop eligibility for Child Benefit regardless of who is claiming. When a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training (or even while in education, if they work those hours), Child Benefit stops.

Let me provide you with a formal assessment based on all the information you've given me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I've completed my assessment:

## Child Benefit Eligibility Decision

### Alex: **Not Eligible**

**Reasons:**

1. **Working 24+ hours per week:** Although Alex is 19 and in approved education (A-levels), he works 24 hours or more per week in paid employment. Under the rules, Child Benefit stops when a child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week.

2. **Another person is already claiming:** Alex's mum is already receiving Child Benefit for him. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at any one time.

---

**What this means:**

Even if Alex's mum were to stop her claim, the fact that Alex works full-time hours (24+ per week) would still mean that neither of you would be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

If Alex's working hours reduce to fewer than 24 hours per week in the future while he's still under 20 and in approved education, it may be worth revisiting eligibility at that time.

I hope this information is helpful. Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?

However, there are two factors that affect eligibility: 1) Alex works 24 hours or more per week in paid employment. According to the rules, Child Benefit stops if a child 'starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training.' The rules indicate that working these hours affects eligibility. 2) Additionally, Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child at any one time. Since someone else is already claiming and Alex works full-time hours (24+ hours per week), the claimant is not eligible to receive Child Benefit for Alex.
